section: Load data and keep only 'station', 'data', and 'species'
end_anchor: dplyr::select(sample_id, major_area, year, month, catch, species_code)
grain_in: STATION_BS: one row per haul (sample_id); bagseine: one row per catch record, at most sample_id x species_code but possibly finer
grain_out: station: one row per haul (sample_id x major_area x year x month); data: one row per catch record
units_out: counts of individuals (catch); identifiers
operation: The region's true first statement is the line load("data.Rdata"), which is excluded from the anchors because it carries a trailing comment; it reads STATION_BS and bagseine from disk. The region then keeps identifier and effort columns from each and restricts the station table to major_area 1:8, described in the comment as the eight major bays, which changes which population the station table describes. The column selections are absorbed as they only narrow columns. Note the bay restriction is applied to station only: data keeps all major_area values, and the restriction reaches the catch data only later, through the left_join on sample_id in the matrix node. It cannot be told from the code alone whether bagseine holds one row per haul x species or several rows (for example per length class), which decides whether the later sum(catch) is a re-aggregation or a no-op.
settings: major_area %in% 1:8; station columns kept = sample_id, major_area, year, month; catch columns kept = sample_id, major_area, year, month, catch, species_code; no year restriction here
na_behavior: filter(major_area %in% 1:8) silently drops rows whose major_area is NA as well as rows outside 1:8; the two causes are not distinguishable afterwards. No handling of NA catch at this stage.

grain_in: one row per catch record
grain_out: one row per catch record, for retained species only
units_out: counts of individuals
operation: Counts, for each species, the number of records with catch > 0 pooled over all bays, years and months (count with wt = a logical sums TRUE as 1), flags species with 5 or fewer such records, and drops them from the catch table. The intermediate vector rare_sp is absorbed because it only carries the species list to the filter. Rarity is defined on the unfiltered catch table, so records from major_area values outside the eight bays contribute to the count even though those bays are dropped downstream.
settings: threshold n <= 5 positive records; positivity defined as catch > 0 (a record of exactly 0 does not count); pooled across all strata rather than within bay, period or season
na_behavior: dplyr's count sums the weight with na.rm = TRUE, so a record with NA catch contributes 0 and is indistinguishable from a true zero or a negative value. A species that appears nowhere in the catch table has no row at all and so is never flagged, never dropped, and never appears downstream.

section: 2 - Sample x species matrix with zeros
grain_in: one row per catch record (retained species)
grain_out: one row per haul (sample_id x major_area x year x month), one column per species
units_out: counts of individuals per haul, zeros included
operation: Sums catch to one value per haul x species, reshapes to a wide haul-by-species matrix filling unobserved combinations with 0, then joins that matrix onto the distinct list of station sampling occasions and replaces the resulting missings with 0. The pivot_wider is absorbed as a reshape; the join and the two zero-fills are the decision, since they are what converts absence of a record into a measured zero. The join direction means hauls present in the catch table but absent from station are dropped, and hauls present in station but absent from the catch table are kept as all-zero rows.
settings: values_fill = 0 in the reshape; replace_na(x, 0) after the join; names_prefix sp_; distinct() on station before joining, which silently deduplicates any repeated sample_id rows; left_join keyed on sample_id alone
na_behavior: Three different situations collapse into the same 0: a species not caught in a haul that was fished, a haul that returned no retained species at all, and a haul listed in station that has no row in the catch table for any reason (not processed, lost, or never fished). Downstream nothing distinguishes them.

section: Period scheme: 11 periods, all 3-year bins over 1992-2024
grain_in: none (constants)
grain_out: one row per calendar year, 1992-2024
units_out: period labels P1-P11
operation: Defines the period scheme and builds the year-to-period lookup: 11 bins of 3 years covering 1992 through 2024, with a stopifnot guard that the bin lengths sum to the span. The label column period_is_partial is set to FALSE for every year and is never read later, so it asserts completeness rather than testing it.
settings: start_year 1992, end_year 2024, period_lengths = rep(3, 11); factor levels fixed at P1..P11; period_is_partial hardcoded FALSE
na_behavior: No missing values are possible here; the stopifnot aborts the script if the bin lengths and the year span disagree.

grain_in: one row per haul, one column per species
grain_out: one row per haul x species (with bay, year, month, date, period, season attached)
units_out: counts of individuals per haul x species
operation: Restricts hauls to 1992-2024, attaches the period label, reshapes the species columns back to long form, builds a date pinned to the 15th of the month, and assigns a season from the calendar month. The reshape and the species_code type conversion are absorbed. The season rule puts December with January and February of the same calendar year, so a Winter stratum is Jan, Feb and Dec of one year rather than a contiguous Dec-to-Feb window; the object is named monthly_sp but one row is still a single haul, not a month.
settings: year >= 1992 and year <= 2024; season cut points DJF/MAM/JJA/SON with Fall as the catch-all TRUE branch; date fixed to day 15; season factor levels Winter, Spring, Summer, Fall
na_behavior: filter(!is.na(period)), commented 'safety', can drop nothing given the preceding year filter and the lookup covering every year in that range. A haul with NA month would fall to the Fall branch of case_when rather than becoming NA, and would give an NA date; that case is not guarded.
notes: Some redundancy in converting species code to integer.

grain_in: one row per haul x species
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season x species
units_out: mu and var in counts per haul and counts squared; I_i is a dimensionless invariability index
operation: Computes, within each bay x period x season x species, the mean and variance of abundance across individual hauls and forms I_i = mu^2 / var. The header comment states that I_i is based on monthly temporal series; this code averages over haul-level rows, not over monthly totals, so the code and the comment disagree. The monthly version is computed separately further down as pop_inv_ps_temporal and is the one used in the portfolio effect, so the file contains two different I_i quantities and this is the one written to population_invariability_<date>.csv.
settings: grouping bay x period x season x species; sample variance (var, denominator n-1); I_i defined only where var > 0; no na.rm, so any NA abundance propagates
na_behavior: I_i is NA when var is 0 (every haul in the stratum gave the same count, including the common case of all zeros) and also when var is NA (fewer than two hauls, or any NA abundance). These distinct causes collapse into a single NA_real_ and are not distinguishable downstream; note that var = 0 means perfect stability, which would be infinite invariability, while var = NA means the quantity is undefined.
notes: A grain size issue, but it only affects e6 and e7 codes. The correction was made and rerun. No qualitative change.

grain_in: one row per haul x species
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season
units_out: mu_C and var_C in counts per month-total and counts squared; I_C is a dimensionless invariability index
operation: Sums abundance over all species and all hauls within a bay x period x season x date to a monthly community total, then takes the mean and variance of those totals across months and forms I_C = mu_C^2 / var_C. The first summarise changes the grain from haul to month and is absorbed into the same region because it exists only to feed the second. Because the monthly total sums over hauls rather than averaging them, its size scales with the number of hauls fished that month, so months of unequal effort are not comparable; the 180-haul filter applied later equalises effort per stratum but not per month.
settings: grouping bay x period x season x date, then bay x period x season; sample variance; I_C defined only where var_C > 0; no na.rm
na_behavior: I_C is NA when var_C is 0 (identical monthly totals) and when var_C is NA (a stratum with a single sampled month, or any NA abundance). Both collapse into one NA_real_ and cannot be told apart in the output file.

grain_in: one row per haul x species
grain_out: sp_monthly: one row per bay x period x season x month x species; sp_var_temporal and sp_set: one row per bay x period x season x species
units_out: abund_date in counts per month; var_i in counts squared
operation: Builds the monthly total per species within each stratum, then the temporal variance of that series per species, and keeps only species whose variance is finite. sp_set is absorbed as a column subset that carries the retained species list forward. The comment calls this 'species with definable temporal variance', but is.finite(var_i) also retains species whose variance is exactly 0, which includes species never caught in the stratum: these are carried into the synchrony denominator, where they add 0 to sum_sd_i but still count as members of the community. Species with a single sampled month get var_i = NA and are the only ones dropped.
settings: na.rm = TRUE inside var; filter is.finite(var_i), which keeps zero variance and drops NA and infinite; the commented Option B alternative filter is not applied
na_behavior: var_i is NA only when the stratum has fewer than two dates for that species; those rows are removed by the filter, so the missingness becomes an absence of rows rather than an NA, and the fact that a species was dropped is not recorded anywhere downstream.

grain_in: one row per bay x period x season x month x species
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season x month
units_in: counts of individuals per month per species
units_out: counts of individuals per month, summed over retained species
operation: Restricts the monthly species series to the retained species set with an inner join and re-sums to a monthly community total, so that the community variance used in synchrony is built from exactly the species whose variances are summed in the denominator. Because the retained set is per stratum, the population being totalled differs from the one totalled in the community invariability node, which uses all species.
settings: inner_join keyed on bay, period, season, species_code, which drops species-months for dropped species and also drops any stratum with no retained species
na_behavior: A stratum where every species was dropped disappears entirely rather than producing an NA total; downstream that is indistinguishable from a stratum that was never sampled.

grain_in: one row per bay x period x season x species (variances); one row per bay x period x season x month (community totals)
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season, in two tables
units_out: sum_var_i and var_C_kept in counts squared, sum_sd_i in counts, n_dates a count of months
operation: Computes the two denominators and the numerator of synchrony per stratum: the sum of species temporal variances, the sum of species temporal standard deviations, and, in the second statement of the region, the variance of the community monthly total together with the number of months contributing. The two statements are kept in one region because they are the matched pieces of a single ratio; they are computed from different inputs and neither is absorbed into the other.
settings: na.rm = TRUE in all three sums and in var; pmax(var_i, 0) guards a negative variance before the square root, which cannot arise from var() and so is inert; n_dates counts rows of the kept community series, that is months with at least one retained species
na_behavior: With na.rm = TRUE, a stratum in which every var_i is NA yields sum_var_i = 0 and sum_sd_i = 0 rather than NA, so an empty stratum and a stratum of perfectly stable species produce the same zeros. var_C_kept is NA when the stratum has a single month.

grain_in: one row per bay x period x season
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season
units_out: phi_var and phi are dimensionless ratios; phi is bounded in [0,1]
operation: Joins the variance pieces and forms two synchrony statistics: the variance ratio var_C / sum(var_i) and the Loreau-de Mazancourt index var_C / (sum(sd_i))^2. The header block documents this output as columns sum_sd_i, var_C and phi_LM; the code names them sum_sd_i, var_C_kept, phi_var and phi, so the documented and actual column names differ.
settings: inner_join on bay, period, season, so strata missing from either side are dropped silently; phi_var defined only where sum_var_i > 0 and phi only where sum_sd_i > 0
na_behavior: phi and phi_var are NA when the corresponding denominator is 0 (no retained species, or all species perfectly stable) and when var_C_kept is NA (a single month). These causes collapse into one NA and are not separable in the output; n_dates is carried through and is the only way to detect the single-month case.

grain_in: one row per haul x species
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season x species
units_out: mu and var in counts per month and counts squared; I_i dimensionless
operation: Recomputes population invariability on monthly totals: sums abundance per species per month, then takes the mean and variance of that monthly series and forms I_i = mu^2 / var. This is the same formula as the earlier pop_inv_ps node but applied to a different input grain (monthly totals rather than individual hauls), so it is a separate quantity and a separate node; only this version feeds the portfolio effect, while only the earlier version is exported.
settings: grouping bay x period x season x date x species then bay x period x season x species; na.rm = TRUE in mean and var, unlike the earlier I_i node; I_i defined only where var > 0
na_behavior: I_i is NA when var is 0 (a flat monthly series, including a species never caught in the stratum) and when var is NA (a single month). Both collapse into NA_real_; the next node then drops both, so a perfectly stable species and an unmeasurable one leave the calculation the same way.

grain_in: one row per haul x species
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season x species
units_out: w is a proportion summing to 1 within a stratum
operation: Builds abundance weights: sums abundance per species per month, averages that monthly total over months to get w_raw, then normalises within the stratum so the weights sum to one. The mean is taken over the months present for that species-stratum combination, which is the same set of months for all species here since the long table carries a row per haul x species; the ungroup and select only carry the result forward and are absorbed.
settings: w_raw = mean of monthly totals, so weighting is by mean abundance rather than by total or by occurrence; na.rm = TRUE throughout; w set to 0 rather than NA when the stratum total is 0
na_behavior: If every species in a stratum has zero mean abundance, all weights are 0 rather than NA, and the stratum then contributes no usable weight downstream; that case is indistinguishable from a species that is genuinely absent, which also gets w = 0.

grain_in: one row per bay x period x season x species
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season
units_out: weighted_mean_I_i dimensionless; n_I_i_used a count of species
operation: Joins weights onto the temporal I_i values and takes the abundance-weighted mean of I_i within each stratum over species that have a finite I_i, a finite weight, and a strictly positive weight, recording how many species were used. Excluding species with NA I_i removes exactly those with zero temporal variance, that is the most stable species, from the mean that forms the portfolio denominator; the count n_I_i_used is the only record of how many were excluded, and it does not say why.
settings: inclusion rule is.finite(I_i) & is.finite(w) & w > 0; weighted.mean with no na.rm needed given the filter; NA_real_ returned when no species qualifies; the species set here is all species in the stratum, not the retained set used for synchrony
na_behavior: weighted_mean_I_i is NA when no species in the stratum passes the inclusion rule, which can mean the stratum is empty, that every species has a flat series, or that every weight is 0. These causes collapse into one NA; n_I_i_used = 0 marks the collapse but not its cause.

grain_in: one row per bay x period x season
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season
units_out: portfolio is a dimensionless ratio; > 1 means the community is more invariable than its average species
operation: Attaches community invariability to the weighted mean population invariability and divides to form the portfolio effect, then stamps a version label. The join takes I_C from comm_inv_ps as it stands at this point in the file, that is before the 180-haul filter is applied to it further down, so the value is the same but the ordering matters if the filter is ever moved. Note the two sides of the ratio are not built from the same species set or the same grain history: I_C comes from monthly totals over all species, the denominator from monthly totals over species with positive weight and non-flat series.
settings: left_join on bay, period, season, so strata with no I_C get NA rather than being dropped; portfolio defined only where weighted_mean_I_i is finite and strictly positive; version string 'Fix 2: Temporal + weighted'
na_behavior: portfolio is NA when the denominator is missing or non-positive and also when I_C is NA (from the zero-variance or single-month cases in the community node). The two collapse into one NA_real_ and the exported file does not carry the reason.

section: Strata counts: identify fully sampled strata
grain_in: one row per haul
grain_out: one row per haul, with period, season and a year-month key attached
units_out: identifiers and labels
operation: Re-derives period, season and a year-month string on the station table so that effort can be counted per stratum. The case_when season block is the same code as in the long-data node applied to a different input, so it is a separate node: if one copy is edited the other will not follow, and the two copies differ already in that this one carries no comments and creates ym.
settings: same year window 1992-2024 and same DJF/MAM/JJA/SON cut points as the long-data node; ym formatted as %d-%02d from year and month, so a December is keyed to its own calendar year while its season is Winter of that year
na_behavior: filter(!is.na(period)) can drop nothing given the year filter and the complete lookup. A haul with NA month falls into the Fall branch rather than becoming NA.

section: Strata counts: identify fully sampled strata
grain_in: one row per haul
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season
units_out: n_samples a count of hauls, n_months a count of distinct year-months, months_observed a text list
operation: Counts sampling effort per stratum: distinct hauls, distinct year-months, and the sorted list of those months as a single string. The counts are taken on the station table, so they describe occasions fished, independently of whether any fish were recorded for them.
settings: n_distinct on sample_id and on ym; months_observed collapsed with ', ' which will contain commas and must be quoted in any CSV export
na_behavior: A stratum with no hauls produces no row rather than a zero, so absence of effort and absence of the stratum from the design are indistinguishable in this table.

section: Strata counts: identify fully sampled strata
grain_in: one row per bay x period x season
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season that is retained
units_out: stratum keys only
operation: Keeps only strata whose haul count is exactly 180 and reduces the table to the stratum keys, which then acts as the inclusion list for every exported result. The test is equality, not a minimum, so a stratum with more than 180 hauls is dropped as well as one with fewer. What 180 represents is not stated in the code; it appears to be a complete design of 3 years x 3 months x 20 hauls, but that cannot be confirmed from the script alone.
settings: threshold n_samples == 180 exactly; n_months is computed but not used in the test, so a stratum with 180 hauls concentrated in fewer months passes
na_behavior: No missing values arise; strata failing the test are removed as rows, and no record of how many were removed is kept.

grain_in: one row per bay x period x season x species
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season x species, fully sampled strata only
units_out: mu, var, I_i
operation: Restricts the exported population invariability table to the fully sampled strata by semi-join, and overwrites pop_inv_ps in place, so the object name no longer refers to the same population it did above. The same semi-join code is applied to four different tables in this section; each is a separate node because the table being filtered is what is being checked.
settings: semi_join keyed on bay, period, season; assignment back onto the same name, which makes the step non-idempotent if the script is re-run from this point
na_behavior: Rows carrying an NA I_i are kept if their stratum qualifies, so the exported file mixes strata that are complete with values that are undefined; nothing marks which is which.

grain_in: one row per bay x period x season
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season, fully sampled strata only
units_out: mu_C, var_C, I_C
operation: Applies the same 180-haul stratum filter to the community invariability table, overwriting comm_inv_ps in place. This happens after portfolio_fix2 has already joined the unfiltered I_C, so the two objects were built from different versions of the same name.
settings: semi_join keyed on bay, period, season; in-place assignment
na_behavior: Rows with NA I_C are kept if the stratum qualifies; the reason for the NA is not recoverable from the exported file.

grain_in: one row per bay x period x season
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season, fully sampled strata only
units_in: sum_var_i, sum_sd_i, var_C_kept, phi, phi_var, n_dates
units_out: same columns, restricted
operation: Applies the same stratum filter to the synchrony table, writing to a new name synchrony_ps rather than overwriting synchrony_fixed. Note the filter counts hauls, while the synchrony statistics were computed over months and over the retained species set, so a stratum can pass the 180-haul test while resting on few months or few species.
settings: semi_join keyed on bay, period, season
na_behavior: Strata whose phi is NA are kept if they have 180 hauls; n_dates is exported alongside and is the only column that helps distinguish a single-month stratum from a zero-denominator one.

grain_in: one row per bay x period x season
grain_out: one row per bay x period x season, fully sampled strata only
units_out: same columns, restricted
operation: Applies the same stratum filter to the portfolio table, writing to a new name portfolio_ps. The four exports that follow, together with results_dir and today_tag, fall outside every region: writing a table to disk does not change what a row means, and the file names are dated at run time.
settings: semi_join keyed on bay, period, season
na_behavior: Strata with NA portfolio are kept if they have 180 hauls; n_I_i_used is carried through and is the only indicator of how thin the denominator was.
